premise: I cashed out my $115,000 401(k) to open a bespoke leather‑journal bindery with my brother, who signed a notarized 40% equity stake and a lifetime of free journals for my book club; after a national stationery retailer offered $690,000 for the studio, he forged a buyout document, sold my share, and handed me a $4,200 ‘bookstore’ credit; I retrieved our original agreement folded into the lining of a hand‑bound journal I’d made for his wedding, proved the forgery, and now run ‘Bound by Fraud Books,’ where he bevels leather covers in a shirt that reads ‘Spilled Ink on Trust’ and every journal’s flyleaf prints his perjury case number.
